interactive.brief: The one thing you should see is 3x + 2x lining up with 5x at every x, because every x-bar stretches together, while 3x + 4 matches 7x only at x = 1, when you slide x.
interactive.title: Like terms
interactive.whatAmILookingAt: A short lesson in fourteen small screens on bars. An x-bar is x long, a length standing for a number you do not know yet, and a slider for x stretches or shrinks every x-bar together. Plain numbers are small squares worth 1 each, and a term taken away is a dashed bar. Two rows sit one above the other to compare, each with its value for the chosen x at its right end. Some screens show an idea and the rest ask you to try it.
interactive.ignores: The values tried for x and the puzzles' numbers are example values, kept to small whole positive numbers so the bars can be drawn and counted. x can be any number, even a negative or a fraction, and every tidy-up here still holds; a bar just cannot be drawn with a negative length. Two letters are drawn together on one screen only, and no powers such as x² are drawn.

numbers.label: Example x = 4: 3x is three x-bars, 3 × 4 = 12, in step 1
With x = 4, 3x is 12, not 7 (3 + 4) or 34 (3 and 4 side by side), in step 2
3x + 2x and 5x both make 35 at x = 7, as 3 sevens and 2 sevens make 5 sevens, in step 3
4x + 3x = 7x, not 12x (counts multiplied) or 7x² (a power made up), in step 4
Example a = 3: 3a + 2a and 5a both make 15, as 3 threes and 2 threes make 5 threes, in step 5
4a + 3b + 2a = 6a + 3b, not 9a (b joined onto a) or 9ab (letters read as objects, every piece counted), in step 6
Sliding x from 1 to 3: 3x + 4 and 7x match only at x = 1, where both make 7, then part, 13 and 21 at x = 3, in step 7
5x + 2 is already finished, not 7x or 7, in step 8
Trying x = 3: 3x + 2x and 5x both make 15; 3x + 4 makes 13 but 7x makes 21, in step 9
Claim 4x + 3 = 7x at x = 2: 4x + 3 makes 11, not 14 (7x) or 7 (4 + 3), in step 10
7x − 2x + 3 − x = 4x + 3, as 7 − 2 − 1 = 4; both make 11 at x = 2, in step 11
−x + 8x + 3 = 7x + 3, not 9x + 3 (starting minus ignored) or 8x + 3 (lone x dropped), in step 12
9x + 4 − 3x − 1 = 6x + 3, not 12x + 5 (minuses ignored) or 6x + 5 (the minus on 1 dropped), in step 13
Three equal resistors of R ohms in series with an example 10 Ω one: 3R + 10, not 13R or R³ + 10, in step 14

explain.text:
A letter stands for a number you do not know yet, so x is a number and 3x means 3 lots of it. Adding 3x and 2x is counting those lots, just as 3 sevens and 2 sevens make 5 sevens.[^1] Picture x as a bar whose length is the number. 3x is three bars end to end and 2x is two more, so together they are five bars, 5x. Change x and every bar changes with it, so the two rows still line up, which is why 3x + 2x = 5x whatever x is. Teachers disagree about the picture. A Bitesize video uses apples,[^2] while NCETM says teaching 3a + 2a = 5a as apples, 'fruit salad algebra', should be avoided,[^3] and treats it as counting lots of a number, as with sevens.[^1] This lesson uses bars, because a letter stands for a number, not an object.

Each part joined on by + or − is a [[term]], and the sign in front of it belongs to it, even a minus at the very start. Terms with the same letters, each raised to the same power, like 3x and 2x, are [[like terms]], and plain numbers are all like terms too.[^4] Only like terms can be added or taken away into one term.[^5] So 3x + 4 is already finished. 7x is 3x and 4x more, so it matches 3x + 4 only when 4x is 4, which is when x is 1. At x = 3, 3x + 4 makes 13 but 7x makes 21. A lone x is 1x, so 7x − 2x + 3 − x is 7 − 2 − 1 = 4 lots of x, plus 3, which is 4x + 3. Resistances in series add, as the total resistance is the sum of the individual resistances,[^6] so three resistors of R ohms and an example 10 Ω one total R + R + R + 10 ohms, which tidies to 3R + 10.

A tidied [[expression]], the whole string of terms, is another way of writing the same thing, as Bitesize says of an expanded bracket: two ways of writing the same expression.[^7] So both give the same value for every number, and you can check a tidy-up by trying one. With x = 2, 7x − 2x + 3 − x makes 14 − 4 + 3 − 2 = 11, and 4x + 3 makes 8 + 3 = 11. One match is not proof, since 3x + 4 and 7x both make 7 at x = 1, so try a second number. A mismatch shows a slip straight away. Turning round R = R₀(1 + αΔT),[^8] the formula in the course's puzzle, needs expressions rewritten without changing their value, and collecting like terms is the first of those moves this course teaches.

**A letter stands for a number, so like terms can be counted together, 3x + 2x = 5x, while 3x + 4 is already finished.[^5] Each sign belongs to the term after it, and trying a number in both versions checks the tidy-up.**

analogy.text: Say a reel holds x metres of cable, a length you have not measured. Three full reels give 3x metres and two more give 2x, so together 5x metres, whatever x turns out to be. Three reels and a 4 m offcut give 3x + 4 metres, and that is as short as it gets until you know x.
analogy.breaks: A reel's length is a positive number of metres, but x can be any number, even a negative number or zero, and 3x + 2x = 5x still holds. Real reels also differ a little, while every x in an expression is exactly the same number.

practice.text:
- Mark each term with the sign in front of it.
- Group the like terms: terms with the same letters and powers together, the plain numbers together.
- Add or take away the counts in each group, with a lone x counting as 1.
- Write the groups side by side, usually letters first.
- Try a number in the old and new versions, then a second number. Avoid 0 and 1, where a slip such as x² for x still matches.

**Rule of thumb:** Same letters, same powers, count them together. Anything else stays side by side.

**Worked example:** 6a + 5 − 2a + 3 − a. The a terms are 6a, −2a and −a, and 6 − 2 − 1 = 3, so 3a. The plain numbers are 5 and 3, which make 8. So the answer is 3a + 8. As a check, with a = 2 the start makes 12 + 5 − 4 + 3 − 2 = 14, and 3a + 8 makes 6 + 8 = 14.

**Common mistakes**
- Joining a letter term to a plain number, so 3x + 4 becomes 7x. Try x = 2: 3x + 4 makes 10, but 7x makes 14.
- Writing 3x + 2x as 5x². x² is x times x, a different term. Try x = 3: 5x makes 15, but 5x² makes 45.
- Dropping a lone x or the minus in front of it, so 8x − x becomes 8x. The lone x is 1x, so it is 7x.
- Ignoring a minus at the start, so −x + 8x becomes 9x. The minus belongs to the lone x, so it is 7x.

views.label: Lots of a number (NCETM)
views.text: NCETM says teaching 3a + 2a = 5a as three apples plus two apples, 'fruit salad algebra', should be avoided, because letters stand for numbers, not objects. It treats collecting like terms as counting lots of a number, as with sevens. This course follows it and draws bars.

interactive.html:
Rows of bars, each x long, and small squares worth 1 each. The values of x are examples.

Only like terms join, and trying two numbers checks a tidy-up.
interactive.title: Like terms
interactive.brief: The one thing you should see is 3x + 2x lining up with 5x at every x, because every x-bar stretches together, while 3x + 4 matches 7x only at x = 1, when you slide x.

checks.label: Collecting like terms generalises unitising in number: three lots and two lots of the same number make five lots of it, whatever the number, so the two rows that compare them line up wherever x is slid

It is incorrect to teach that 3a + 2a = 5a because three apples plus two apples make five apples ('fruit salad algebra'): the screen that names both views draws a as a length, a number, so 3a + 2a and 5a end together and make 15 at a = 3, and the two-letter puzzle names reading letters as objects as a slip
Terms are like terms if they have the same variables and exponents, and all constant terms are like terms: each tidy-up joins only those, and each puzzle accepts only its own tidy answer

Terms can be combined only if they have the exact same variable portion: a letter term and a plain number never join, and the row that holds them lines up with the joined-up version at just one value of x

The worked numbers: 3x makes 12 at x = 4; 3x + 2x and 5x make 35 at x = 7 and 15 at x = 3; 3x + 4 and 7x make 7 at x = 1 but 13 and 21 at x = 3; 4x + 3 makes 11 and 7x makes 14 at x = 2; 7x − 2x + 3 − x and 4x + 3 both make 11 at x = 2
Every tidy answer gives the same value as its question for every x tried, whole, a half or negative, and every wrong answer offered gives a different value at the x drawn
The total resistance is the sum of the individual resistances: three resistors of R ohms and an example 10 Ω one in series total R + R + R + 10, which tidies to 3R + 10 for every R tried

Each wrong answer offered is the one a named slip gives: 3 and 4 added or written side by side, the counts multiplied, a power made up, a plain number joined onto the letters, the letter dropped, the other side of a claim worked out, a starting minus ignored, a lone x dropped, every minus ignored, the minus on a plain number dropped, or letters read as objects with every piece counted
Every picture is drawn to count: each bar is x long and each square 1, so a row ends at its value; a right answer lines up with its question and a wrong one does not
Before an answer, nothing in a puzzle's picture shows the answer
Every demonstration has finished arriving within 4.5 s of its screen opening, none starting before the 0.35 s screen fade ends; every answer's motion, right or wrong, within 2.5 s

applied.problem: Research marks the apples picture as contested and NCETM's document says it should be avoided because letters stand for numbers, not objects; 'picture this in different ways' hides that. 'Same letter' also misleads for terms with several letters (IR₁, IR₂ in i3).

'Same letter, same power' fails for terms with several letters met later (IR₁ and IR₂ share I but are not like terms); and checking at 0 and 1 hides the listed 5x² slip, since 5x² and 5x match at both.

notes.problem: contested is null and confidence 'settled', yet the research marks the apples-versus-number picture as contested (Bitesize video vs NCETM core concept 1.4); the maths itself is settled, but the contested field could carry both views.

The resistor screen (3R + 10) rests on series resistances adding, which no kept source states (textbook-standard) and whatAmILookingAt does not describe; labels count steps 1 to 12 while the step control runs 0 to 11.
